title: Average sensitivity of threshold functions
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's proof (2026) of the asymptotic Gotsman-Linial conjecture: every polynomial threshold function of degree at most d on the n-dimensional Boolean cube has average sensitivity at most 8 d sqrt(n). The first lesson sets up the cube, proves that symmetric examples attain the order d sqrt(n), and proves a one-sided coupling inequality for equally distributed random variables. The second builds a grading operator weighted by an arbitrary positive function and shows that its anticommutator with a sign function counts the edges on which the sign is constant. The third combines parity, the vanishing of low blocks and a binomial coupling into the theorem, and derives a bound on noise sensitivity.
prerequisites: core course Linear Algebra; foundations-of-von-neumann-algebras lesson hilbert-spaces-and-compact-operators (Theorem 2.2, projection theorem; Section 3, adjoints), used in finite dimensions
